record.original_question: Find necessary and sufficient conditions for a primitive skew lattice, defined in the source as a skew lattice that is both distributive and cancellative, to be embedded into a ring. If not every primitive skew lattice is embeddable, determine the resulting requirement that every primitive subalgebra of an embeddable skew lattice must also be embeddable. More generally, characterize when skew chains A > B > C, A > B > C > D, or longer skew chains can be embedded into a ring.

evidence.quote: In particular, find necessary and sufficient conditions for a primitive skew lattice to be embedded into a ring.
A primitive skew lattice is both distributive and cancellative, Perhaps all primitive skew lattices can be so embedded.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A skew lattice is an algebra $(S; \wedge, \vee)$ with two associative idempotent binary operations satisfying the absorption identities $x \wedge (x \vee y) = x = x \vee (x \wedge y)$ and $(x \wedge y) \vee y = y = (x \vee y) \wedge y$. A skew lattice is called distributive if it satisfies $x \wedge (y \vee z) \wedge x = (x \wedge y \wedge x) \vee (x \wedge z \wedge x)$ and $x \vee (y \wedge z) \vee x = (x \vee y \vee x) \wedge (x \vee z \vee x)$; it is called cancellative if $x \vee y = x \vee z$ together with $x \wedge y = x \wedge z$ implies $y = z$, and dually. Green's preorder on a skew lattice is defined by $a \geq b$ iff $a \wedge b = b = b \wedge a$ and $a \vee b = a = b \vee a$. A primitive skew lattice is a skew lattice that is both distributive and cancellative and that, with respect to Green's preorder, consists of exactly two comparable $\mathcal{D}$-classes $A > B$. A skew chain $A > B > C > \cdots$ is a skew lattice whose $\mathcal{D}$-class structure under Green's preorder forms a finite chain of the indicated length.

Given any (not necessarily commutative) ring $R$, the operations $x \wedge y := xy$ and $x \vee y := x + y - xy$ make the set of idempotents of $R$ closed under these operations only in special cases, and any subset closed under $\wedge$ and $\vee$ in this sense forms a skew lattice; such a skew lattice is said to be embeddable into a ring.

(a) Determine necessary and sufficient conditions for a primitive skew lattice to be embeddable into a ring.

(b) If not every primitive skew lattice is embeddable, characterize embeddable skew lattices via the condition that each primitive subalgebra must itself be embeddable, and determine whether this local condition is also sufficient.

(c) More generally, determine necessary and sufficient conditions for a finite skew chain $A > B > C$, $A > B > C > D$, or longer, to be embeddable into a ring.
artifact.status_search_result: No published resolution was located. The problem appears in a collection of open problems posed at NCS 2018 on noncommutative structures, and web searches did not turn up subsequent literature establishing necessary and sufficient ring-embeddability conditions for primitive skew lattices or for general skew chains of length three or more. The status appears to remain open.
